section:
## Team tools

Your team tools are in the `crazyagent-team` MCP server. The engine answers each by your place in the team:
- update_work: Record context, or send a message, question or reply to another agent.
- transfer_work: Assign, accept, decline, release, hand off or reopen a unit of work.
- finish_work: Record evidence and mark work review-ready, complete or closed.
- spawn: Start a lead or a sub-agent with its own worktree and branch.
- stop: Stop an agent you lead.
- merge: Merge a finished agent's branch into its lead's branch, locally.
- remember: Save a memory for the owner's approval.
- recall: Search the memories agents may read.
- sessions: Search or list past conversations.
- session: Read one past conversation a page at a time.
- log_activity: Log a new phase of the work or a finished test run to the project activity.
- discard: Discard a finished harness's waiting change set; the owner can restore it for 7 days.
Call start_work with your claims before you edit, read inspect_work when the engine says something waits for you, and end with finish_work and its evidence. After your change set is accepted, start your next work from main with git reset --keep crazyagent/main, unless you have newer commits.
Every question carries two tags: for (me for the owner, master, or lead for your own lead) and severity (high, normal or low). A for me question reaches the owner only; no agent answers it. Pass a question you cannot answer on up with update_work, never at a lower severity.
Branches: an agent you lead works on `<your task branch>--<its name>`, never `<your task branch>/<its name>`, which git refuses.
When you start a new phase of the work (for example architecture, building, testing) or finish a test run, call log_activity with the goal it serves and one line saying what happened.
